newsitem.title: USA: Ill. school bill to be introduced to House panel.
newsitem.headline: Ill. school bill to be introduced to House panel.

text.p: Illinois House Speaker Michael Madigan will introduce a proposed school financing reform and bond issuance package to the revenue committee Wednesday for discussion, his spokesman said.
Madigan has not decided whether the plan promoted by Gov. Jim Edgar will be brought to the House floor today for a vote, spokesman Steve Brown said.

The proposal calls for a 25 percent income tax increase to generate $600 million for schools, $900 million of property tax cuts. The infusion of money would be used to bring spending in less affluent districts up to a minimum of $4,225 per pupil.
It would also use $100 million of growth in state revenues for a matching school construction bond program of up to $2 billion of bonds from the state and a like amount from participating districts.
House Republicans led by Minority Leader Lee Daniels have consistently opposed the plan, however, contending that school funding could be increased using revenue growth and other taxes.

Madigan had planned to bring the proposal to a vote by last Friday, but opted to delay consideration to this week, leading a spokesman for Daniels to argue that the speaker did not have enough votes to get it through the House.
Republican Senate President James "Pate" Philip has proposed a lesser increase in the income tax and increased teacher accountability.
Philip is "anxiously awaiting it," according to spokeswoman Patty Schuh.
The proposal calls for increasing the income tax rate from 3.0 percent to 3.75 percent, which would generate about $1.5 billion.
